1: # Minimal translation from accepted NL0
2: 
3: Start with the accepted source map and specification. Read the supplied proof
4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.
7: 
8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.
11: 2. Choose the mathematical representation, complete original H/E input types,
12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies
13:    source paragraphs and note locations. Mathlib is freely available; retain an
14:    M port only when useful, otherwise apply the library directly. Supply short
15:    `endpoint_correspondence` notes for every E and complete P (including all
16:    hypotheses), explaining direct or equivalent translation. Save partial interface drafts, revise
17:    those drafts, and use small Lean probes for uncertain types. Do not restart
18:    from an empty interface after an ordinary error.
19: 3. Type-check source correspondence, dependency boundaries and the complete
20:    interface, then obtain a separate independent semantic interface review.
21:    Normal full/translation entry dispatches no proof worker before its actual
22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:
37:    inherit the actual pre-proof semantics after checking full endpoint types,
38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens
39:    B-final. Faithful drift is warning-qualified; a nonpass waits for the user's
40:    explicit delivery/recheck/translation-reset choice. Invalid proof is never
41:    semantically overridden.
42: 
43: ## Background notes are references, not extra ports
44: 
45: New contracts select `source.background_mode: node_local_reference`. Original
46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains
47: hash-bound. Do not turn every note into a new M root, retype its entire library
48: signature, or require an extra theorem merely to restate it. The frozen
49: stage-one text's historical `background.effective` expansion is still supported
50: as `promoted_inputs` for old contracts; it is not the new translation default.
51: 
52: At the pre-freeze semantic review and final Audit B, notes are guidance, not library permissions. All proved results in
53: the pinned Mathlib environment are available without registration. Review every
54: external E and complete P against its actual Lean type using the concise author
55: correspondence explanation; independently check direct or equivalent meaning.
56: A new external assumption or stronger hypothesis still returns to the source
57: boundary. See [the complete Audit B standard](audit-b.md).
58: 
59: ## Work continuously, report genuine blockers
60: 
61: There is no ordinary `TASK_INCOMPLETE` reporting tool. While unfinished, keep
62: making concrete edits, queries or proof checks. Submit a completed artifact or
63: report a supported mathematical/source/input blocker. If a model turn ends
64: without either, the controller sends one short continuation instruction; it
65: does not demand a progress essay. State/usage recording is programmatic.
66: Proof workers follow [structured diagnosis and repair](proof-repair.md): report
67: actual packet obstructions. Progress counters are passive; no idle-turn count
68: cancels sibling work or authorizes interface changes.
69: 
70: Whole-case/stage execution, total tokens and calls are unlimited by default.
71: Each native check has the configured 180-second wall limit and finite Lean
72: heartbeat policy. Keep measuring usage and allow explicit
73: cancellation. Only a user-requested finite case deadline covers the entire
74: translation, including preparation, queue waiting, parallel proofs, assembly
75: and Audit B; later stages cannot reset that optional deadline. Preserve partial
76: results and report execution health separately from mathematical acceptance.

value.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
value.conclusion: dimH(G)=dimH(E)+1, where E has its original Euclidean metric and G is E×[0,1] identified with Euclidean Rn(n₀+1) as specified in the selected target; this holds for every natural n₀, including n₀=0. Both sides are finite, so the equality also holds for real Hausdorff dimensions.

hypotheses.origin: problem.md:16–23; approved addition stated at lines 16–19.

hypotheses.statement: E is compact in Euclidean ℝ^n₀.

definitions.type: family of Euclidean real normed spaces indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For each natural m, Rn(m)=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), namely real m-tuples with norm (Σ_{h<m}|x_h|²)^(1/2). For m=0 this is the one-point zero vector space.

definitions.type: extended diameter of a subset of an emetric space
definitions.definition: For an emetric space W and B⊆W, ediam(B)=sup{edist(x,y):x,y∈B} in ℝ≥0∞; the empty supremum is zero.

definitions.type: real diameter of a bounded subset of a metric space
definitions.definition: For a bounded subset B of a metric space W, diam(B)=sup{dist(x,y):x,y∈B}, with diam(∅)=0. Its cast to ℝ≥0∞ is ediam(B). This notation is used only after boundedness has been established.

For an emetric space W, B⊆W, real a and r∈ℝ≥0∞, content(a,r,B)= inf_{U:ℕ→Set W} inf_{B⊆⋃i U_i} inf_{∀i ediam(U_i)≤r} Σ'_i sup_{h:U_i nonempty} ediam(U_i)^a. Infima and sums take values in ℝ≥0∞. A failed condition has empty infimum ∞; the supremum over a nonemptiness proof is zero for an empty member. This is exactly BasisObjects.content in basis-registry.json /lean_header.

For a metric space W, B⊆W, a>0 and δ>0, C^a_δ(B)=content(a,ENNReal.ofReal δ,B). The original real-diameter convention is the infimum of Σ_i diam(U_i)^a over countable covers of B with diam(U_i)≤δ, empty members contributing zero. The proof establishes compatibility of these two formulations.

binders.type: countable family of subsets of W

definitions.type: unnormalized Hausdorff measure evaluated on a set
definitions.definition: For a Borel emetric space W, B⊆W and real a, H^a(B)=MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a B. This is the metric outer-measure construction with gauge r↦r^a and no dimensional prefactor, taking values in ℝ≥0∞.

binders.type: emetric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of an emetric space
definitions.definition: For an emetric space W and B⊆W, dimH(B)=sup{d∈ℝ≥0 : H^d(B)=∞}, interpreted in ℝ≥0∞, using the Borel structure of W. This is Hausdorff dimension and gives dimH(∅)=0. A finite dimension can be represented by its nonnegative real value; we explicitly establish finiteness before doing so.
I=[0,1], the closed unit interval in ℝ.
For a metric space W, MaxProd(W)=W×ℝ with distance max(dist(x,y),|t-u|) between (x,t) and (y,u). For real normed W this is its usual maximum product norm.

definitions.type: family of real normed spaces indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: L2Prod(m)=WithLp 2 (Rn(m)×ℝ), with the library L² product norm and its induced metric.
For every natural m, euclideanLift m=WithLp.toLp 2 on Rn(m)×ℝ; it is the identity on underlying pairs. This is exactly the definition in the frozen basis header.

definitions.type: family of coordinate concatenation maps L2Prod(m)→Rn(m+1)
definitions.definition: For each natural m, j(m)(p) is the (m+1)-tuple whose first m coordinates are those of p.fst and whose last coordinate is p.snd. This defines a total coordinate concatenation map.
F=E×I, regarded during the cover argument as a subset of MaxProd(Rn(n₀)).
D=dimH(E), with E in its original Euclidean Rn(n₀) metric.
T=dimH(F), using the maximum product metric.
G consists of coordinate concatenations (x_0,…,x_{n₀-1},t) with x∈E and t∈I. This is exactly E×[0,1] under the original target's specified identification with Euclidean ℝ^(n₀+1).

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on the real line
definitions.definition: volume denotes Lebesgue measure on the Borel measurable space ℝ, with values in ℝ≥0∞.

definitions.type: set indicator with a zero outside branch
definitions.definition: For a set B⊆W and function f:W→ℝ≥0∞, indicator(B,f)(t)=f(t) for t∈B and 0 otherwise. We write 1_B(t)c for indicator(B,constant c)(t), including c=∞; this uses a zero branch outside B.

lintegral(μ,f)=∫⁻ t,f(t)∂μ is the supremum of the integrals of nonnegative measurable simple functions below f, for a measure μ on a measurable space W and f:W→ℝ≥0∞. No finiteness of the value is implicit.

value.representation_notes: n is the original natural n₀, including zero; E remains a subset of BasisObjects.Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Ordinary X × ℝ uses Mathlib's maximum product metric. WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) uses the L² product metric: here 2 is the extended nonnegative real exponent, not the coordinate count. EuclideanSpace is PiLp 2 over Fin n. The explicit j appends the last real coordinate with Fin.snoc and unj truncates at castSucc and reads Fin.last; T009 proves this is a bijective isometry. G is exactly the set of coordinate concatenations of E and I, as an image under these explicit functions, in Euclidean Rn(n+1). E001 transports dimension from the maximum product to the L² product; no unproved metric identification is definitional. H fixes the canonical Borel measurable structure locally, avoiding any extra measurability premise on X or A. content is the exact frozen basis definition; powers are ENNReal real powers, infima/suprema and nonnegative sums remain in ℝ≥0∞ with ∞ allowed. cost retains the nonempty-member supremum; for positive exponents an empty member costs zero. RealCover explicitly includes boundedness before using real diameters, and realCost uses their nonnegative finite casts. Cover is the finite extended-diameter condition, equivalent to RealCover at positive real scales. N004 supplies finiteness before any use of NNReal representatives or toReal; standard cast order/addition compatibility does not add an assumption. No M premise ports or background-note premise ports are introduced. The pinned product metric instances require Fact (1 ≤ p): this is a proof that the Lp exponent lies in the metric range, and at p=2 it is supplied by the library, not an additional project hypothesis. The pinned Prod.dist_eq is max of the coordinate distances. Fin n indexes exactly the initial n coordinates; Fin.castSucc preserves their values in Fin(n+1), and Fin.last n is the appended coordinate. In cost and content, ^ a has real exponent a on ENNReal; in the squared-distance formulas ^ 2 is the ordinary natural square of a real distance.

steps.statement:
∀ (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] (A : Set X) (a : ℝ), 0 < a →
  (∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
    BasisObjects.content a (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A =
      ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : RealCover δ A U), realCost a U) ∧
  (∀ (ι : Type*) [Countable ι] (V : ι → Set X),
    ∃ e : ι ↪ ℕ, ∃ U : ℕ → Set X,
      (∀ k, U (e k) = V k) ∧
      (∀ i, i ∉ Set.range e → U i = ∅) ∧
      (⋃ i, U i) = (⋃ k, V k) ∧
      cost a U = cost a V ∧ realCost a U = realCost a V) ∧
  (∀ δ₁ δ₂ : ℝ, 0 < δ₁ → δ₁ ≤ δ₂ →
    BasisObjects.content a (ENNReal.ofReal δ₂) A ≤
      BasisObjects.content a (ENNReal.ofReal δ₁) A) ∧
  (∀ (δ : ℝ) (U : ℕ → Set X), 0 < δ → Cover δ A U →
    BasisObjects.content a (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A ≤ cost a U) ∧
  (∀ (δ : ℝ) (b : ℝ≥0∞), 0 < δ →
    (∀ U : ℕ → Set X, Cover δ A U → b ≤ cost a U) →
      b ≤ BasisObjects.content a (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A) ∧
  (H a A = ⨆ (δ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < δ), BasisObjects.content a (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A) ∧
  (∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → BasisObjects.content a (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A ≤ H a A) ∧
  (∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
    (BasisObjects.content a (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A = 0 ↔
      ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ U : ℕ → Set X, Cover δ A U ∧ cost a U < ENNReal.ofReal ε)) ∧
  (H a A = 0 ↔
    ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      ∃ U : ℕ → Set X, Cover δ A U ∧ cost a U < ENNReal.ofReal ε)
steps.explanation: Complete N001 package: identify the guarded extended-diameter infima with bounded real-diameter covers at positive scale; explicitly reindex arbitrary countable families with empty padding and equal union/cost; prove scale monotonicity, both infimum bounds, positive-real-scale supremum, and the two zero/cheap-cover equivalences. Use the pinned hausdorffMeasure_apply formula directly with the Borel structure fixed by H. No measurability or boundedness of A is assumed; the empty admissible family has infimum ∞. Strict inequalities compare with ofReal ε only when ε>0.

steps.statement:
∀ (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] (A : Set X) (q : ℝ), 0 < q → H q A = 0 →
  ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    ∃ U : ℕ → Set (X × ℝ), Cover δ (A ×ˢ I) U ∧ cost (q + 1) U < ENNReal.ofReal ε
steps.explanation: Existing upper covering construction only. At r=min(1,δ), take the q-cost <ε/4 cover from N001; add positive numerical radii with geometric q-cost ≤ε/4, without changing sets. The radii are at most r and one. Subdivide I into ceil(1/r_i) closed intervals, use the maximum metric and N_i≤2/r_i, then reindex the countable family of finite products. The obligation retains all positive scale/tolerance quantifiers and allows empty and zero-diameter members.

steps.statement:
∀ (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] (A : Set X) (q : ℝ), 0 < q → H q A = 0 →
  H (q + 1) (A ×ˢ I) = 0 ∧
  ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    ∃ U : ℕ → Set (X × ℝ), Cover δ (A ×ˢ I) U ∧ cost (q + 1) U < ENNReal.ofReal ε
steps.explanation: Export full N002: retain T002's covers and apply N001's zero-measure equivalence at exponent q+1 in X×ℝ. This closes the temporary scale/tolerance assumptions; no dimension or compactness condition is used.

steps.statement:
∀ (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] (A : Set X) (s δ : ℝ),
  0 < s → 0 < δ → ∀ V : ℕ → Set (X × ℝ), Cover δ (A ×ˢ I) V →
    BasisObjects.content s (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A ≤ cost (s + 1) V
steps.explanation: For an arbitrary product cover, derive boundedness from its finite diameter bound, project the sets, and enclose each nonempty real projection by its closed [inf,sup] hull (empty members use ∅). Hulls are Borel, contain the projections, and have volume at most the member diameter. The selected projected sets cover each fibre t∈I. Integrate the resulting indicator inequality over ℝ. The series interchange uses a.e. measurability of each nonnegative indicator summand; no finiteness or integrability is required. Keep c and every series in ℝ≥0∞, including c=∞. Apply the direct library interval measure, lintegral monotonicity, lintegral_tsum and indicator-constant formulas with their actual conditions. For the zero-diameter power identity use s>0.

steps.statement:
∀ (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] (A : Set X) (s : ℝ), 0 < s →
  (∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
    BasisObjects.content s (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A ≤
      BasisObjects.content (s + 1) (ENNReal.ofReal δ) (A ×ˢ I)) ∧
  H s A ≤ H (s + 1) (A ×ˢ I)
steps.explanation: Export full N003 by the lower-infimum bound of N001 applied to T004, even when there is no admissible cover. Take suprema over positive real scales at exponents s and s+1 to obtain the Hausdorff-measure inequality. Both inequalities are unconditional in finiteness and require no measurability of A or covering sets.

steps.statement:
0 ≤ dimH E ∧ dimH E ≤ (n : ℝ≥0∞) ∧ (n : ℝ≥0∞) < ⊤ ∧
  1 ≤ dimH (F n E) ∧ dimH (F n E) ≤ (n : ℝ≥0∞) + 1 ∧
  dimH E < ⊤ ∧ dimH (F n E) < ⊤ ∧ dimH I = 1 ∧
  ∃ d k : ℝ≥0, (d : ℝ≥0∞) = dimH E ∧ (k : ℝ≥0∞) = dimH (F n E) ∧ 1 ≤ k
steps.explanation: Export N004 using coordinate bases to get finrank n and n+1 (including the empty basis at n=0), direct Mathlib full-space dimension and monotonicity, and the interval interior dimension formula. A point of E supplied by H001 gives the isometric fibre t↦(x,t), hence T≥1. The finite ENNReal bounds yield the stated NNReal representatives; casts preserve order and addition of finite values by the ordinary library identities. The chosen point does not escape. The quantified representatives are NNReal values d,k; their real coercions give d_real,k_real, and their ENNReal coercions recover D,T without any truncation.

steps.statement: dimH (F n E) ≤ dimH E + 1 ∧ dimH E < ⊤ ∧ dimH (F n E) < ⊤
steps.explanation: Export N005. Choose the finite representatives from N004. For every real q>d, q>0; apply the critical-exponent zero-measure theorem to E at the NNReal exponent determined by q, N002, and the dimension upper bound from measure ≠∞. A contrary strict upper inequality is refuted at the source midpoint q=(d+k-1)/2. Cast the resulting finite-real inequality back to ENNReal. The direct library critical-exponent declarations quantify NNReal exponents, so positivity supplies the needed nonnegative subtype and its real coercion.

steps.statement:
dimH (F n E) = dimH E + 1 ∧ dimH E < ⊤ ∧
  dimH (F n E) < ⊤ ∧ dimH E + 1 < ⊤
steps.explanation: Export N006 on the original domain. For the finite real representatives d,k, handle d=0 using the fibre bound k≥1. If d>0 and k<d+1, use the source midpoint s=(k-1+d)/2; it is positive, less than d, and s+1>k. The critical-exponent infinite-measure theorem, N003 and the dimension lower bound from infinite measure contradict this. Antisymmetry with N005 gives equality. N004 gives finiteness and includes n=0. H002 remains an original project premise although this source argument does not use compactness.

steps.statement:
Isometry (j n) ∧ Function.Bijective (j n) ∧
  Function.LeftInverse (unj n) (j n) ∧ Function.RightInverse (unj n) (j n) ∧
  j n '' (BasisObjects.euclideanLift n '' F n E) = G n E ∧
  ∀ (x y : Rn n) (t u : ℝ),
    (dist (j n (BasisObjects.euclideanLift n (x,t)))
      (j n (BasisObjects.euclideanLift n (y,u)))) ^ 2 =
      (∑ h : Fin n, |x h - y h| ^ 2) + |t - u| ^ 2 ∧
    (dist (BasisObjects.euclideanLift n (x,t))
      (BasisObjects.euclideanLift n (y,u))) ^ 2 =
      (∑ h : Fin n, |x h - y h| ^ 2) + |t - u| ^ 2
steps.explanation: Export full N007 in the fixed Euclidean representations. Split squared L² product norm into its two coordinate norms and expand the Euclidean norm as the finite coordinate sum; split the concatenated sum at Fin.last. Equal squares of nonnegative distances give Isometry j. Check both composites with the explicit truncation/last-coordinate unj, and identify the image set. The last conjunct records the squared-distance identity for all x,y,t,u. n=0 is retained with an empty initial sum. The metric bridge is a proved obligation, not a definition of an isometry.

steps.statement: dimH (G n E) = dimH E + 1 ∧ dimH E < ⊤ ∧ dimH (G n E) < ⊤
steps.explanation: Instantiate the exact E001 port at n and S=F n E to transport dimH from the maximum product to its L² image. Apply isometry invariance to j from N007 and its explicit image G, then use N006. This gives the complete target equality and transfers finiteness to G. H001 and H002 remain the exact original nonempty/compact assumptions in the exported project theorem; no positivity assumption on n is introduced.

import Mathlib
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology
open Set MeasureTheory
namespace BasisObjects
abbrev Rn (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
noncomputable def content {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X]
    (s : ℝ) (r : ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i)
    (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ r),
      ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s
def euclideanLift (n : ℕ) : Rn n × ℝ → WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2
end BasisObjects

namespace IntervalProduct
abbrev Rn := BasisObjects.Rn
def I : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
def F (n : ℕ) (E : Set (Rn n)) : Set (Rn n × ℝ) := E ×ˢ I
def j (n : ℕ) (p : WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ)) : Rn (n + 1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => p.fst i) p.snd)
def unj (n : ℕ) (v : Rn (n + 1)) : WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin n => v i.castSucc), v (Fin.last n))
def G (n : ℕ) (E : Set (Rn n)) : Set (Rn (n + 1)) :=
  j n '' (BasisObjects.euclideanLift n '' F n E)
noncomputable def H {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  letI : MeasurableSpace X := borel X
  letI : BorelSpace X := ⟨rfl⟩
  MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a A
noncomputable def cost {ι X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (U : ι → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ a
noncomputable def realCost {ι X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (U : ι → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑' i, (ENNReal.ofReal (Metric.diam (U i))) ^ a
def Cover {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
def RealCover {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ (∀ i, Bornology.IsBounded (U i)) ∧ ∀ i, Metric.diam (U i) ≤ δ
end IntervalProduct
open IntervalProduct

source.source_statement:
For every n≥0 and every S⊆Rn(n)×ℝ equipped with the maximum product norm, euclideanLift n sends S to an equal-dimensional set in WithLp 2 (Rn(n)×ℝ). This is the identity on underlying pairs and equips the target with the Euclidean product norm.
Closed basis type:
∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Set (BasisObjects.Rn n × ℝ)),
  dimH (BasisObjects.euclideanLift n '' S) = dimH S
Prepared proof:
intro n S
exact YuiBasis.B005 (BasisObjects.Rn n × ℝ) (WithLp 2 (BasisObjects.Rn n × ℝ))
  (WithLp.prodContinuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ (BasisObjects.Rn n) ℝ).symm S
source.context: Both factors are real normed spaces. prodContinuousLinearEquiv is a continuous linear equivalence from WithLp 2 (Rn(n)×ℝ) to the ordinary maximum-norm product. Its inverse has underlying map WithLp.toLp 2. ContinuousLinearEquiv.dimH_image, with scalar field ℝ, gives the displayed equality for every set and every natural n, without original H or measurability of S. No textbook result is assumed.
source.qualification: Prepared adapter from the explicitly supplied basis, retaining its exact permitted E statement. Its reduction is the inverse product continuous linear equivalence followed by the proved dimension-invariance theorem. It is not an imported class-3 project lemma. The source theorem and map identity have been read at the pinned commit; native basis checks remain separate from mathematical review.

The successful M015 probe confirms the latter full signature at commit 905b95818eb32af7874a58b427f50c1711a5e96c. No mismatch of norm direction, map, domain, codomain or parameter range was found.

value.statement: dimH(G)=dimH(E)+1, where E has its original Euclidean metric and G is E×[0,1] identified with Euclidean Rn(n₀+1) as specified in the selected target; this holds for every natural n₀, including n₀=0. Both sides are finite, so the equality also holds for real Hausdorff dimensions.

E001.explanation: The closed type is copied exactly from prepared B011: every natural n and every set S in the ordinary maximum-norm product are quantified, with no nonempty, compact or measurable assumption. BasisObjects.euclideanLift n is exactly WithLp.toLp 2, the inverse of the library product continuous linear equivalence; its codomain carries the L² product norm. No extra external statement is assumed.

P.explanation: The parameters are every natural n (including zero) and every subset E of the original Euclidean Rn n; H001=E.Nonempty and H002=IsCompact E are preserved in the exported conditional theorem. G n E is, by its explicit j/image definition, exactly all (n+1)-coordinate concatenations of x∈E and t∈[0,1], with EuclideanSpace's L² metric. T009 proves the intervening L²-product/coordinate-space isometry, and E001 supplies the distinct maximum-product dimension change. The terminal asserts dimH G=dimH E+1 and finiteness of both dimensions in ℝ≥0∞; since addition and order on these finite values agree with their nonnegative real representatives, this is also the original real Hausdorff-dimension equality. Conversely the full source conclusion includes the same finiteness, so its real equality casts to this terminal proposition. No assumption or case n=0 is lost.

results.value: n is the original natural n₀, including zero; E remains a subset of BasisObjects.Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Ordinary X × ℝ uses Mathlib's maximum product metric. WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) uses the L² product metric: here 2 is the extended nonnegative real exponent, not the coordinate count. EuclideanSpace is PiLp 2 over Fin n. The explicit j appends the last real coordinate with Fin.snoc and unj truncates at castSucc and reads Fin.last; T009 proves this is a bijective isometry. G is exactly the set of coordinate concatenations of E and I, as an image under these explicit functions, in Euclidean Rn(n+1). E001 transports dimension from the maximum product to the L² product; no unproved metric identification is definitional. H fixes the canonical Borel measurable structure locally, avoiding any extra measurability premise on X or A. content is the exact frozen basis definition; powers are ENNReal real powers, infima/suprema and nonnegative sums remain in ℝ≥0∞ with ∞ allowed. cost retains the nonempty-member supremum; for positive exponents an empty member costs zero. RealCover explicitly includes boundedness before using real diameters, and realCost uses their nonnegative finite casts. Cover is the finite extended-diameter condition, equivalent to RealCover at positive real scales. N004 supplies finiteness before any use of NNReal representatives or toReal; standard cast order/addition compatibility does not add an assumption. No M premise ports or background-note premise ports are introduced. The pinned product metric instances require Fact (1 ≤ p): this is a proof that the Lp exponent lies in the metric range, and at p=2 it is supplied by the library, not an additional project hypothesis. The pinned Prod.dist_eq is max of the coordinate distances. Fin n indexes exactly the initial n coordinates; Fin.castSucc preserves their values in Fin(n+1), and Fin.last n is the appended coordinate. In cost and content, ^ a has real exponent a on ENNReal; in the squared-distance formulas ^ 2 is the ordinary natural square of a real distance.

result.text:
1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: For the optional [basis route](../../nl0/references/basis.md), this same Audit B
4: checks the conditional intermediate under the frozen basis interfaces. It is
5: followed by b2lean's fresh inspection of the actual `YuiClosed.P`, with only
6: original H and explicitly approved class 4 remaining. Its final receipt binds
7: the compiled standalone source and full actual signature/dependency closure;
8: this intermediate receipt must not be reported as unconditional completion.
9: 
10: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
11: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
12: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
13: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
14: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
15: 
16: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
17: 
18: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
19: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
20: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
21: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
22: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
23: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
24: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
25: 
26: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
27: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
28: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
29: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
30: 
31: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
32: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
33: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
34: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
35: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
36: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
37: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
38: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
39: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
40: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
41: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
42: 
43: ## Author correspondence explanations
44: 
45: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
46: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
47: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
48: line-by-line formalization commentary:
49: 
50: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
51:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
52: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
53:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
54:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
55: 
56: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
57: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
58: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
59: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
60: 
61: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
62: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
63: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
64: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
65: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
66: 
67: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
68: 
69: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
70: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
71: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
72: row, then these four global checks:
73: 
74: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
75:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
76: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
77:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
78:    no external inputs, record that fact.
79: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
80:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
81:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
82: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
83:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
84:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
85: 
86: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
87: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
88: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
89: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
90: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
91: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
92: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
93: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
94: 
95: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
96: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
97: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
98: 
99: ## Freely available Mathlib
100: 
101: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
102: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
103: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
104: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
105: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
106: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
107: permissions to use a library theorem.
108: 
109: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
110: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
111: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
112: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
113: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
114: require returning to the affected source boundary.
115: 
116: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
117: 
118: ### Compact review materials
119: 
120: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
121: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
122: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
123: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
124: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
125: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
126: expected type for the actual inspected type.
127: 
128: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
129: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
130: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
131: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
132: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
133: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
134: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
135: 
136: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
137: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
138: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
139: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
140: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
141: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
142: 
143: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
144: 
145: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
146: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
147: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
148: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
149: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
150: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
151: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
152: 
153: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
154: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
155: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
156: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
157: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
158: 
159: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
160: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
161: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
162: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
163: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
164: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
165: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
166: 
167: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
168: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
169: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
170: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
171: review have separate recorded outcomes.
172: 
173: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
174: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
175: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
176: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
177: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
178: scoped development verdict. A whole source with an actual conditional Audit A
179: can yield `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL` after all the same native and semantic checks.
180: It retains the exact source warnings and never upgrades them to full PASS.
181: Neither proves external publications in Lean or
182: establishes formalizer speedup. Preserve failures and report actual costs.

value.text: Fix X,A,a and assume L1: a>0. Work with X's Borel structure, so M001 applies and gives H^a(A)=sup_{r>0} content(a,r,A) over extended nonnegative r. For arbitrary δ, temporarily assume L2: δ>0. At the finite scale ofReal δ, every admissible covering member has finite extended diameter, hence is bounded and has ediam equal to its real diameter cast to ℝ≥0∞. The nonemptiness-proof supremum in D004 is the displayed diameter power on a nonempty member and is zero on an empty member. For a>0 this agrees with assigning the empty member diameter zero and 0^a=0. Thus the nested infima are exactly the original admissible-cover infimum, with no prefactor. A finite family can be padded by empty sets. For an arbitrary countable index type choose an injection into ℕ; at each image index put the unique original member and elsewhere put ∅. This preserves the union and all nonnegative sums. Conversely an ℕ-family is countable. Discharge L2 after this finite-scale interpretation, retaining its δ>0 antecedent for every δ. For arbitrary δ₁,δ₂, temporarily assume L3: 0<δ₁≤δ₂. Every δ₁-cover is a δ₂-cover, so C^a_δ₂(A)≤C^a_δ₁(A). Discharge L3 and quantify the two scales. Every cost bounds its infimum above; a lower bound on every admissible cost bounds the infimum below. If the admissible family is empty its infimum is ∞, and the latter assertion remains true. For any positive extended scale r, if it is finite it is the cast of a positive real scale. The content at r=∞ is at most that at any fixed finite positive scale, since every finite-scale cover is also an ∞-cover. Hence the ∞ scale adds nothing to the supremum. We have proved H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0}C^a_δ(A), and each such content is ≤H^a(A).

For the arbitrary δ,ε, temporarily assume L4: δ>0 and ε>0. Suppose L5: C^a_δ(A)=0. if every admissible cost were ≥ε, the lower-bound property in F001 would imply C^a_δ(A)≥ε>0, a contradiction. Thus an admissible cover of cost <ε exists. Discharge L5 to obtain the forward implication. In terms of the nested infima in D004, any failed cover or diameter condition has value ∞ and cannot give a value <ε, so the approximation provides an actual admissible family. Conversely assume L6: for every positive tolerance there exists an admissible cover of smaller cost. This forces the nonnegative content to be zero: a positive value, finite or infinite, has some positive finite real below it, contradicting the upper bound by those costs. Discharge L6, then L4, and quantify the arbitrary positive scale and tolerance. This proves the zero-content approximation equivalence for every positive scale. These arguments also cover an empty admissible family, whose content is ∞.

By F001, H^a(A)=0 implies each positive-scale content is zero; F002 then gives the required arbitrarily small covers at every scale. Conversely, those covers make every positive-scale content zero by F002, and their supremum is zero by F001. This proves the full equivalence and all asserted content properties. Discharge L1 to retain a>0 as an antecedent and universally quantify X,A,a and the scale/tolerance variables. No boundedness or measurability assumption on A is used.

Fix X,A,q and assume L1: q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix arbitrary real δ,ε and assume L2: δ>0 and ε>0. Put r=min(1,δ), so 0<r≤1 and r≤δ. By N001 with exponent q, scale r and tolerance ε/4 there exists a countable r-cover U of A whose total q-cost is <ε/4; reindex it as a sequence with empty padding if necessary. In particular its members have finite diameter.

Choose U from F001 and put d_i=diam(U_i), with d_i=0 on empty members. For each natural i define a_seq(i)=min(r,(ε·2^(-i-3))^(1/q)). Both entries of this minimum are positive, so 0<a_seq(i)≤r and a_seq(i)^q≤ε·2^(-i-3). The nonnegative geometric series has sum Σ_{i≥0}2^(-i-3)=1/4 (its partial sums are (1/4)(1-2^(-m)) for the first m terms). Hence Σ a_seq(i)^q≤ε/4. Put r_i=max(d_i,a_seq(i)). Then 0<r_i≤r≤1 and r_i^q=max(d_i^q,a_seq(i)^q)≤d_i^q+a_seq(i)^q. Summing nonnegative terms, using F001 and the geometric bound, gives Σ r_i^q<ε/2. Numerical padding changes no covering set and works even if X is a singleton.

For each natural i put N_i=ceil(1/r_i), a positive integer. Then 1/N_i≤r_i and N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i, since 0<r_i≤1. The closed intervals [h/N_i,(h+1)/N_i], 0≤h<N_i, cover I. Define W_seq(i,h)=U_i×[h/N_i,(h+1)/N_i]. In the maximum product metric any two points of this product have distance at most r_i, since the first-coordinate diameter is d_i≤r_i and the second-coordinate interval length is 1/N_i≤r_i. The product family covers A×I, and its index set {(i,h):i∈ℕ,0≤h<N_i} is countable. Empty products have zero cost. By N001 this countable family may be reindexed into ℕ without changing the union or sum. It is a δ-cover, and its total (q+1)-cost is at most Σ_i N_i r_i^(q+1)≤2Σ_i r_i^q<ε. The power cancellation r_i^(q+1)/r_i=r_i^q is valid because r_i>0. Rearranging these nonnegative sums is legitimate, and the upper bound is finite.

F003 holds for arbitrary positive δ,ε. Discharge L2 to obtain existence of the stated arbitrarily fine arbitrarily cheap covers. Since q+1>0, N001, now for MaxProd(X), A×I and exponent q+1, implies H^(q+1)(A×I)=0. Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,q. This proves the output proposition on the whole asserted domain without any positive-diameter assumption on the covering sets.

Fix X,A,s,δ and assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Set c=C^s_δ(A), possibly ∞. Take any sequence V and assume L2: V is a δ-cover of A×I in MaxProd(X). Put ρ_i=diam(V_i), A_i=π_X(V_i), B_i=π_ℝ(V_i). Every V_i is bounded, since its extended diameter is ≤δ<∞. Each projection has pairwise distances at most ρ_i, whence diam A_i≤ρ_i and diam B_i≤ρ_i≤δ. For a nonempty V_i, B_i is nonempty and bounded above and below: choose any one of its points and use the finite diameter bound. Thus inf B_i and sup B_i exist as real numbers. Put J_i=[inf B_i,sup B_i]. The least-upper-bound and greatest-lower-bound properties give B_i⊆J_i and sup B_i-inf B_i≤ρ_i: for every b,b'∈B_i one has b-b'≤ρ_i, and taking supremum in b then infimum in b' preserves the inequality. In particular inf B_i≤sup B_i. For empty V_i put ρ_i=0 and A_i=B_i=J_i=∅. Each J_i is a closed real interval or ∅, hence Borel measurable, and all projection bounds remain valid. This construction imposes no measurability on V_i or its projections.

For each nonempty member, apply M009 with endpoints inf B_i and sup B_i. By F001, volume(J_i)=ofReal(sup B_i-inf B_i)≤ρ_i. For an empty member volume(J_i)=volume(∅)=0=ρ_i by the empty-set axiom of a measure. Also I=[0,1] is closed and measurable and M009 with endpoints 0,1 gives volume(I)=1. Since I∩J_i⊆J_i, measure monotonicity gives volume(I∩J_i)≤volume(J_i)≤ρ_i; each intersection is measurable as an intersection of closed measurable sets.

Define g(t)=1_I(t)c and f_seq(i)(t)=1_{I∩J_i}(t)ρ_i^s. Fix any real t. In the case L3: t∈I, the family consisting of A_i when t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise covers A: under the auxiliary antecedent L4: x∈A, L2 supplies an i with (x,t)∈V_i, so x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. This proves membership in the projected union; discharge L4 and quantify x. Each such projected set has diameter ≤ρ_i≤δ by F001. N001 therefore gives c≤Σ_i ρ_i^s 1_{J_i}(t)=Σ_i f_seq(i)(t). Discharge L3 after the inside-I argument. If t∉I, g(t)=0 and every f_seq(i)(t)=0 by the indicator zero branch, so the same inequality holds. Universal introduction in t gives g≤Σ_i f_seq(i) pointwise on ℝ, also if c=∞. F002 shows that every indicator summand is Borel measurable: its only values are a nonnegative constant and zero on complementary measurable pieces, hence it is also volume-almost-everywhere measurable. No product of an undefined infinite real quantity is used.

Integrate F003 over ℝ with Lebesgue measure. M011 gives lintegral(volume,g)≤lintegral(volume,Σ_i f_seq(i)). M012 for I and constant c, together with volume(I)=1 from F002, gives lintegral(volume,g)=c·1=c, even when c=∞. M010 for the countable family f_seq exchanges the nonnegative series and lower integral, since F003 established almost-everywhere measurability of each summand. M012 for I∩J_i and constant ρ_i^s evaluates each term. Thus
c=c·volume(I)
 ≤Σ_i ρ_i^s volume(I∩J_i)
 ≤Σ_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i)
 ≤Σ_i ρ_i^s ρ_i
 =Σ_i ρ_i^(s+1).
The middle bounds use F002 and monotonicity of multiplication and nonnegative sums. Each ρ_i is finite and nonnegative, and ρ_i^s·ρ_i=ρ_i^(s+1) holds for positive ρ_i by the real-power law and for ρ_i=0 because s>0. This is an ℝ≥0∞ computation; neither c nor the series need be finite. Discharge L2: every admissible δ-cover has (s+1)-cost at least c.

By the lower-infimum bound in N001, F004 implies C^s_δ(A)≤C^(s+1)_δ(A×I), including if no admissible product cover exists. This holds at every δ>0. Taking suprema over positive scales and using N001 for both positive exponents s and s+1 gives H^s(A)≤H^(s+1)(A×I). Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,s and the scale. These are the complete scale and measure inequalities asserted in the output proposition.

Define e_h=e_basis(h) by the standard coordinate formula: its h-th coordinate is 1 and every other coordinate is 0. The n₀ coordinate unit vectors form a real basis of Rn(n₀): every vector is its finite coordinate linear combination, and equality of coordinates forces all coefficients in a zero combination to vanish. There are n₀ vectors. For n₀=0 this is the empty basis of the zero vector space. In MaxProd(Rn(n₀)), the n₀ vectors (e_h,0) together with (0,1) similarly span uniquely, by the first coordinates and last coordinate, so its real dimension is n₀+1. Both are real normed vector spaces (the second with the maximum product norm) and finite dimensional. Apply M007 to their full spaces and M006 to E⊆univ Rn(n₀) and F⊆univ MaxProd(Rn(n₀)). We obtain 0≤D≤n₀ and 0≤T≤n₀+1. The lower zero bounds follow from the ℝ≥0∞ codomain of dimH. Thus D and T are finite, including when n₀=0. A finite extended nonnegative real is the cast of its unique nonnegative real representative, and casts preserve finite sums and order.

The real line has basis {1}, hence real dimension one. The set I=[0,1] contains the open interval (0,1) in its interior: for each of its points the distance to the two endpoints has a positive minimum, giving a contained open ball. In particular 1/2 belongs to the interior. Apply M013 to the real normed space ℝ and A=I. Its hypotheses hold and it gives dimH(I)=1.

H001 supplies x_f∈E. Define f_f(t)=(x_f,t). For any real t,u, the maximum product distance between f_f(t) and f_f(u) is max(dist(x_f,x_f),|t-u|)=|t-u|. Thus f_f is an isometry; its image of I is {x_f}×I, a subset of F by x_f∈E.

Apply M008 to f_f and I, using the isometry in F003. It gives dimH(f_f '' I)=dimH(I)=1 by F002. Apply M006 to f_f '' I⊆F, also in F003, to get 1≤dimH(F)=T. Combining with F001 proves 0≤D≤n₀<∞ and 1≤T≤n₀+1<∞, together with dimH(I)=1 and the finite real identifications. The chosen point and its map do not occur in the output proposition.
By N004, write D and T as casts of finite real values d_real≥0 and k_real≥1, respectively. Order and addition of these finite values agree with their real operations.

Fix arbitrary real q and assume L1: q>d_real. F001 gives q>0, so q defines a nonnegative real exponent. M003 with set E and exponent q gives H^q(E)=0, since dimH(E)=D<q. Apply N002 to X=Rn(n₀), A=E and q. Its positive-exponent and zero-measure premises have just been established, and E×I in MaxProd(Rn(n₀)) is F. Therefore H^(q+1)(F)=0.

Since q+1>0, it is also a nonnegative real exponent. By F002 its Hausdorff measure on F is zero, hence different from ∞. Apply M004 with F and exponent q+1. It gives T≤q+1, equivalently k_real≤q+1 by F001. Discharge L1: for every real q>d_real one has k_real≤q+1.

Assume for contradiction L2: k_real>d_real+1. Put q_mid=(d_real+k_real-1)/2. Then d_real<q_mid<k_real-1, because k_real-1>d_real. F003 with q=q_mid gives k_real≤q_mid+1<k_real, a contradiction. Discharge L2 to obtain k_real≤d_real+1. Cast back by F001: T≤D+1. Finiteness is already supplied by F001. This proves the output proposition for every natural n₀, including zero.

By N004 write D,T as casts of real values d_real≥0 and k_real≥1. Their orders and addition agree with real operations. If L3: d_real=0, the fibre bound k_real≥1 gives k_real≥d_real+1. Discharge L3 to retain this implication. Since d_real≥0, the other case is d_real>0.

Assume L1: d_real>0. To prove the lower bound, assume for contradiction L2: k_real<d_real+1. Then 0≤k_real-1<d_real by F001. Put s_mid=(k_real-1+d_real)/2. These inequalities imply 0<s_mid<d_real and k_real<s_mid+1. The strict positivity of s_mid follows from d_real>0 even if k_real-1=0.

By F002, M002 applied to E at the nonnegative exponent s_mid gives H^s_mid(E)=∞, because dimH(E)=D is the cast of d_real. N003, applied with X=Rn(n₀), A=E and s=s_mid, gives H^s_mid(E)≤H^(s_mid+1)(F). Consequently H^(s_mid+1)(F)=∞.

M005 with A=F and the nonnegative exponent s_mid+1 yields s_mid+1≤T from F003, equivalently s_mid+1≤k_real by F001. This contradicts F002. Discharge L2 and conclude k_real≥d_real+1 under L1. Discharge L1, and combine with the d_real=0 implication in F001 by exhaustive cases on d_real≥0. Hence k_real≥d_real+1 for all cases.

F004 gives T≥D+1, and N005 gives T≤D+1. Antisymmetry proves T=D+1. Both dimensions and their sum are finite by F001 and N004. When n₀=0, N004 forces D=0 and the fibre branch already supplies the lower bound; the upper proof also covered this case. This proves the output proposition. Compactness remains an original hypothesis in the global specification, although this replacement proof does not use it.

Fix arbitrary p,z∈L2Prod(n₀). Apply M014 with W=Rn(n₀), Z=ℝ and argument p-z. These are normed additive commutative groups, hence satisfy its seminormed assumptions. With the coordinatewise subtraction and distance as norm of difference, the source gives
 dist(p,z)²=‖p.fst-z.fst‖²+|p.snd-z.snd|²
 =Σ_{h<n₀}|p.fst_h-z.fst_h|²+|p.snd-z.snd|².
The second equality uses the defining squared Euclidean norm on Rn(n₀). On the other hand, the defining squared norm on Rn(n₀+1), split into its first n₀ coordinates and last coordinate, gives
 dist(j(n₀)(p),j(n₀)(z))²=Σ_{h<n₀}|p.fst_h-z.fst_h|²+|p.snd-z.snd|².
The two nonnegative distances have equal squares; hence they are equal. These formulas hold also when n₀=0, with an empty finite sum.

By F001, j(n₀) is an isometry. Its explicit inverse sends a vector v∈Rn(n₀+1) to the pair consisting of its first n₀ coordinates in Rn(n₀) and its last coordinate, regarded as an element of L2Prod(n₀) using euclideanLift n₀. Coordinate evaluation shows that both composites are the identity. Hence j(n₀) is bijective. By the definitions of F,G,euclideanLift and j, a point of j(n₀) '' (euclideanLift n₀ '' F) is precisely a concatenation of x∈E and t∈I; conversely every such concatenation arises this way. Thus this image equals G. For arbitrary x,y∈Rn(n₀) and real t,u, specialize F001 with p_bound=euclideanLift n₀ (x,t) and z_bound=euclideanLift n₀ (y,u) to obtain the squared-distance formula stated in the output proposition for every such x,y,t,u. For n₀=0 the inverse still extracts the last coordinate and the empty initial tuple; every step is unchanged.

Apply the exact prepared basis port E001 with its universally bound n equal to the current n₀ and S=F⊆MaxProd(Rn(n₀)). Its identity map on underlying pairs is euclideanLift n₀, with image in L2Prod(n₀). It gives dimH(euclideanLift n₀ '' F)=dimH(F)=T. This is exactly the registered maximum-to-L² product dimension equality.

N007 proves that j(n₀):L2Prod(n₀)→Rn(n₀+1) is an isometry and that j(n₀) '' (euclideanLift n₀ '' F)=G. Apply M008 with this map and set euclideanLift n₀ '' F. It gives dimH(G)=dimH(euclideanLift n₀ '' F). By F001 and N006 this equals T=D+1=dimH(E)+1. N006 also provides finiteness. By D016, G is exactly the specified Euclidean E×[0,1] under coordinate concatenation, and E on the right retains its original Euclidean Rn(n₀) metric. N007 includes the n₀=0 identification, so there is no excluded ambient dimension. Since the dimensions are finite, the extended nonnegative equality is also equality of the real Hausdorff dimensions. This is the complete selected conclusion.

1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144: 
145: If the first series is infinite the desired inequality is immediate;
146: otherwise let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Take the infimum over the
147: arbitrary covers to obtain (1). As its left side is unbounded at small
148: scales, \(H^{s+1}(F)=\infty\), giving \(\dim_H F\geq s+1\).
149: Letting \(s\uparrow D\) proves \(\dim_H F\geq D+1\).
150: 
151: ### Lower bound when \(D=0\)
152: 
153: Choose \(x_0\in E\). The map \(t\mapsto(x_0,t)\) is an isometric
154: embedding of \([0,1]\) into \(F\), so dimension monotonicity gives
155: \(\dim_H F\geq\dim_H[0,1]\). This interval has dimension one:
156: equal-length covers gave the upper bound above. For \(0<s<1\), any
157: \(\delta\)-cover with diameters \(\rho_i\leq\delta\) satisfies
158: \(\sum_i\rho_i\geq1\). To see this, enclose its nonempty members
159: in open intervals of lengths at most \(\rho_i+\varepsilon2^{-i-1}\),
160: use countable subadditivity of length to get
161: \(1\leq\sum_i\rho_i+\varepsilon\), and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
162: Hence \(\sum_i\rho_i^s\geq\delta^{s-1}\sum_i\rho_i
163: \geq\delta^{s-1}\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
164: This proves the lower bound one. Thus \(\dim_H F\geq1=D+1\),
165: including when \(n=0\).
166: 
167: Together the bounds establish the required equality.
168: 
169: ## Input status
170: 
171: This file fixes the problem, conventions and supplied proof route for future
172: tests. It is a natural-language input, not an NL0 artifact, an Audit A receipt,
173: a Lean proof, or a passing test result. Future runs must independently produce
174: and check those artifacts. The basic Hausdorff-measure and integration facts
175: used here must be registered by that future NL0/Audit A workflow.

27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144: 
145: If the first series is infinite the desired inequality is immediate;
146: otherwise let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Take the infimum over the
147: arbitrary covers to obtain (1). As its left side is unbounded at small
148: scales, \(H^{s+1}(F)=\infty\), giving \(\dim_H F\geq s+1\).
149: Letting \(s\uparrow D\) proves \(\dim_H F\geq D+1\).
150: 
151: ### Lower bound when \(D=0\)
152: 
153: Choose \(x_0\in E\). The map \(t\mapsto(x_0,t)\) is an isometric
154: embedding of \([0,1]\) into \(F\), so dimension monotonicity gives
155: \(\dim_H F\geq\dim_H[0,1]\). This interval has dimension one:
156: equal-length covers gave the upper bound above. For \(0<s<1\), any
157: \(\delta\)-cover with diameters \(\rho_i\leq\delta\) satisfies
158: \(\sum_i\rho_i\geq1\). To see this, enclose its nonempty members
159: in open intervals of lengths at most \(\rho_i+\varepsilon2^{-i-1}\),
160: use countable subadditivity of length to get
161: \(1\leq\sum_i\rho_i+\varepsilon\), and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
162: Hence \(\sum_i\rho_i^s\geq\delta^{s-1}\sum_i\rho_i
163: \geq\delta^{s-1}\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
164: This proves the lower bound one. Thus \(\dim_H F\geq1=D+1\),
165: including when \(n=0\).
166: 
167: Together the bounds establish the required equality.
168:

1: Basis proof for the complete selected target. All Hausdorff measures below are unnormalized diameter measures: no dimensional prefactor, ball-radius convention, probability normalization, or new hypothesis is introduced. The only H is the original one: n is an arbitrary natural number and E⊆Euclidean ℝ^n is nonempty and compact. Write X=Rn(n), I=[0,1], F=E×I, and D=dim_H E. We use the maximum metric on X×ℝ during the covering argument and return to the required Euclidean metric in paragraph 8. The original proof route is replaced only as recorded in the replacements array. The B statements are dependencies with proofs/reductions, not a permission list restricting the freely available pinned Mathlib.

3: 1. Content and normalization (B101 from B001). For a>0 and δ>0 let C^a_δ(A) be the infimum of Σ_i(diam U_i)^a over countable δ-covers of A. In Lean this is BasisObjects.content a (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A. A set with extended diameter ≤δ<∞ is bounded, and its extended diameter is the cast of its real diameter. Empty sets contribute zero: the header explicitly uses the supremum over a nonemptiness proof, which is zero when empty and is the unique displayed value when nonempty. This also agrees with 0^a=0 for a>0. A finite cover may be padded by empty sets. A cover with any countable index type can be enumerated with empty padding after an injection into ℕ, and conversely an ℕ-family is countable. The sums are unchanged. Thus these contents coincide exactly with those in the original problem. No normalizing constant occurs.
4: 
5: The admissible covers for δ₁≤δ₂ form nested families, giving C^a_δ₂≤C^a_δ₁. Each admissible cover bounds the infimum above. A bound from below for every admissible cover bounds its infimum below, also when there are no admissible covers (infimum of the empty family is ∞). B001 identifies H^a with the supremum of these contents over positive extended scales. Scales ∞ add nothing: content at ∞ is at most the content at any fixed finite positive scale. Every finite positive extended scale is the cast of a positive real scale. Hence H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0} C^a_δ(A), exactly the problem's convention. In particular every finite-scale content is ≤H^a.
6: 
7: 2. Approximation of a zero content (completion of B101). In the complete lattice ℝ≥0∞, if the infimum of a family is zero then for every finite ε>0 some family member is <ε; otherwise ε is a positive lower bound. Apply this to the nested infima over U and the cover and diameter conditions. An unsuccessful condition has empty infimum and value ∞, so a value <ε provides an actual admissible U. Conversely covers of arbitrarily small positive cost make the content zero. Taking the supremum over δ proves: H^a(A)=0 iff at every positive scale there are countable covers of arbitrarily small positive a-cost. All costs and sums are interpreted in ℝ≥0∞; finite estimates can equivalently be written in nonnegative reals.
8: 
9: 3. Upper cover construction (B102). Let X be any metric space, A⊆X, q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix a target scale δ>0 and ε>0. Put r=min(1,δ)>0. By paragraph 2 choose a countable r-cover U_i with Σ d_i^q<ε/4, where d_i=diam U_i (zero for empty sets). Choose numbers 0<a_i≤r with a_i^q≤ε 2^(-i-3). For example take the minimum of r and (ε 2^(-i-3))^(1/q); all quantities are positive. Then Σ a_i^q≤ε/4, since Σ_{i≥0}2^(-i-3)=1/4. Put r_i=max(d_i,a_i). These numbers satisfy 0<r_i≤r≤1, and r_i^q=max(d_i^q,a_i^q)≤d_i^q+a_i^q. Summing gives Σ r_i^q<ε/2. This numerical padding handles zero-diameter singletons in every metric space, including X=ℝ^0; no replacement ball or additional ambient point is required.
10: 
11: Let N_i=ceil(1/r_i), a positive integer. The intervals [j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i], 0≤j<N_i, cover I and have length 1/N_i≤r_i. Also N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. The products U_i×[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i] cover A×I. Their diameters in the maximum metric are at most r_i, because both coordinate distances are at most r_i. Empty products have cost zero. The index set {(i,j):i∈ℕ, j<N_i} is countable, so this is an admissible countable cover at scale δ. Its total (q+1)-cost is at most Σ_i N_i r_i^(q+1)≤2 Σ_i r_i^q<ε. The equality r_i^(q+1)/r_i=r_i^q is legitimate since every r_i>0. As δ and ε were arbitrary, paragraph 2 gives H^(q+1)(A×I)=0.
12: 
13: 4. Lower slicing construction (B103). Let X be any metric space, A⊆X, s>0 and δ>0. Set c=C^s_δ(A), with c allowed to be ∞. Take any countable δ-cover V_i of A×I in the maximum product metric. For a nonempty V_i let ρ_i=diam V_i, A_i=π_X(V_i), and B_i=π_ℝ(V_i). Coordinate distances do not exceed product distances, so diam A_i≤ρ_i≤δ and diam B_i≤ρ_i. A nonempty B_i is bounded above and below, because it has finite diameter; define J_i=[inf B_i,sup B_i]. The defining least-upper-bound and greatest-lower-bound inequalities show B_i⊆J_i. They also show sup B_i-inf B_i≤ρ_i: every b-b' with b,b'∈B_i is ≤ρ_i, then take the supremum in b and infimum in b'. Consequently J_i is a measurable closed interval and B007 gives volume J_i≤ρ_i. For empty V_i put ρ_i=0, A_i=B_i=J_i=∅; all these conclusions still hold. Notice that this does not assert measurability of V_i, A_i or B_i.
14: 
15: For any t∈I, the family consisting of A_i when t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise is a δ-cover of A. Indeed (x,t) lies in some V_i whenever x∈A, and then x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Therefore
16: c≤Σ_i ρ_i^s 1_{J_i}(t) for every t∈I.
17: Equivalently, on all of ℝ,
18: 1_I(t)c ≤ Σ_i 1_{I∩J_i}(t)ρ_i^s.
19: Outside I both sides are zero; this also works for c=∞ because indicator functions use a zero branch, avoiding any ambiguous real multiplication. Every I∩J_i is measurable. Integrate this inequality with Lebesgue measure. B009 gives monotonicity, B010 evaluates the indicators, B007 gives volume I=1, and B008 exchanges the nonnegative series and lower integral. The result is
20: c=c·volume I
21:  ≤Σ_i ρ_i^s volume(I∩J_i)
22:  ≤Σ_i ρ_i^s volume J_i
23:  ≤Σ_i ρ_i^s ρ_i
24:  =Σ_i ρ_i^(s+1).
25: Indicator summands are measurable, hence AEMeasurable as required by B008. The second inequality uses inclusion and the monotonicity of a measure. All powers are nonnegative; ρ_i is finite; the power identity holds also for ρ_i=0 because s>0. These inequalities hold in ℝ≥0∞, and do not require c or the series to be finite. Taking the infimum over the arbitrary covers gives C^s_δ(A)≤C^(s+1)_δ(A×I). Taking suprema over δ and using paragraph 1 gives H^s(A)≤H^(s+1)(A×I).

27: 5. Finite dimensions and the fibre bound (part of B104). By B003 and B004,
28: 0≤D≤dimH(X)=finrank ℝ X=n.
29: The rank equality follows from the n standard Euclidean coordinate vectors; for n=0 it is the empty basis. Thus D is finite and may be identified with its nonnegative real value without changing addition or order. The same argument in X×ℝ gives dimH F≤n+1<∞ in the maximum norm; its coordinate basis has n+1 vectors.
30: 
31: The set I has nonempty real interior: (0,1)⊆interior I and, for example, 1/2 belongs to it. B012 with finrank ℝ ℝ=1 gives dimH I=1. Choose x₀∈E using the original nonemptiness assumption. The map t↦(x₀,t) is an isometry for the maximum product metric, since max(dist(x₀,x₀),|t-u|)=|t-u|. B006 and B003 therefore give dimH F≥dimH({x₀}×I)=1. This also proves the entire required lower bound when D=0.
32: 
33: 6. Upper dimension inequality (part of B104). For any real q>D, we have q>0. Regard q as a nonnegative real when invoking B002. Its critical-exponent zero conclusion gives H^q(E)=0. Paragraph 3 gives H^(q+1)(F)=0, so this measure is not ∞ and B002 gives dimH F≤q+1. This holds for every q>D. Because D and dimH F are finite, it implies dimH F≤D+1: if dimH F>D+1, choose q strictly between D and dimH F-1, contradicting dimH F≤q+1. No assumption n≥1 has been made, so this includes n=0.
34: 
35: 7. Lower dimension inequality (completion of B104). If D>0, choose any real s with 0<s<D. B002 gives H^s(E)=∞. Paragraph 4 gives H^(s+1)(F)≥H^s(E)=∞, so H^(s+1)(F)=∞. B002 now yields dimH F≥s+1. Together with the fibre bound this implies dimH F≥D+1: if instead dimH F<D+1, the fibre bound gives dimH F-1≥0, and one can choose s strictly between dimH F-1 and D, a contradiction. If D=0, paragraph 5 already gives dimH F≥D+1. Combined with paragraph 6 this proves the maximum-norm equality for every n and the original nonempty compact E. Compactness is retained as H even though the replacement cover argument needs no further use of it.

37: 8. Return to the specified Euclidean target (B105). The header defines euclideanLift n as the identity on pairs into WithLp 2 (Rn(n)×ℝ). Its underlying function is exactly euclideanLift, and it proves that every image set has the same Hausdorff dimension as in the maximum norm. This is an explicit metric-change justification, valid for all n≥0 and all sets.

39: B013 shows that the norm in this new space satisfies ‖(x,t)‖²=‖x‖²+|t|². Apply it to differences. In Rn(n), the squared Euclidean norm is Σ_{j<n}|x_j|² by the defining Euclidean norm. Consequently coordinate concatenation j(x,t)=(x₀,…,x_(n-1),t) has
